A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of in-context learning in Evo2 and Qwen3. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching v1 Appendix E to v3 Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on 100 bitstring transformations, including model accuracy, scaling trends, task-complexity analyses, and error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds Evo2-7B promoter-classification experiments with a label-permutation control in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The original models and bitstring procedure are unchanged. Appendix E adds a classification-specific inference adaptation: nucleotide buffers and class-label runs, with predictions selected by lower perplexity over the candidate label run.

E1.justification: v3 extends evaluation beyond synthetic bitstring transformations to human_nontata_promoters, a native genomic task classifying 251-nucleotide human sequences as promoters or non-promoters. This adds substantially different data and task requirements.

E2.justification: The new promoter comparison includes a 50% random-guessing reference in Figure 6. The original bitstring comparison retains the same Evo2 and Qwen3 models and mode baseline; no new trained comparator is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a promoter-specific protocol using training-set demonstrations, held-out test sequences, randomized nucleotide-label mappings, candidate-label scoring, and a shot sweep reaching 256. The original bitstring evaluation settings, model sizes, and exact-match metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a 16-shot label-permutation ablation testing whether promoter accuracy depends on correctly labeled demonstrations. Section 5 also newly reports sensitivity to using literal binary digits in Qwen3 prompts. Existing BitLoad, BitDiversity, regression, and understandable-mistake analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E adds saturated-power-law fitting and R-squared assessment for promoter scaling, supplementing the existing linear-regression analyses. The original eight Monte Carlo trials, 5,000-replicate bootstrap, and significance tests remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantive native-task findings: Evo2-7B promoter accuracy rises from 48.2% at one shot to 63.6% at 16 and 68.6% at 256; permuting 16-shot labels reduces accuracy to 50.2%. Original bitstring results, including every Table 4 entry, are unchanged. These are new-task results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The ICL formulation, BitLoad definition, global accuracy expressions, BitDiversity definition, and understandable-mistake criterion are retained. Connecting BitLoad to relevant features adds attribution and explanation, without revising its mathematics. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims of emergent genomic ICL and support for a modality-general account. The introduction presents promoter classification as further validation of those claims, rather than redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 expands the existing comparability caveat to discuss StripedHyena2's possible architectural advantage, explicitly acknowledge prompting bias toward Evo2, and describe Qwen3's benefit from familiar binary symbols. It also explains why native promoter validation is excluded from the cross-model comparison.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly documents tokenizer vocabulary, context windows, pretraining token counts, and architecture differences for the existing models. Appendix E specifies 24-nucleotide buffers and label runs and the scoring region. These are added disclosures and task-specific details; the code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of zero-shot forecasting, Chronos 2, Bio-xLSTM, and genomic token-copying research. Additional citations support the promoter dataset, benchmark-design rationale, and BitLoad attribution. The central positioning around emergent versus explicitly trained ICL remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted expansions to related work, model-selection explanations, and discussion; reformats model-selection reasons as an enumerated list; and adds acknowledgments and publication information. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the promoter-performance Figure 6, adds shaded bands to Figure 1's curves, and redraws or resizes existing result plots. Several figures are repositioned and the BitDiversity appendix is renumbered. Existing tables and the detailed appendix plot contents are retained.

improvement.justification: The native promoter experiment and label-permutation control strengthen evidence beyond synthetic bitstrings, while expanded model documentation and comparability caveats improve transparency. The gain is limited by validation on one model and one biological task, with evaluation sample counts and standard-error computation unspecified. The original findings remain intact.
